title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
signature: lowestCommonAncestor(root: TreeNode, p: TreeNode, q: TreeNode) -> TreeNode
statement: Given a BST and two different nodes p and q in it, return their lowest common ancestor: the lowest node that has both as descendants (a node counts as a descendant of itself). (The checker passes the nodes found by value and reads the returned node's value.)

hints.1_question: In a BST, where must the LCA be relative to p and q's values compared with the current node's value?
hints.2_nudge: Start at the root. If both values are smaller go left; if both are larger go right; otherwise the current node splits them (or equals one of them) and is the LCA.
hints.3_big_hint: while cur: if p.val < cur.val and q.val < cur.val: cur = cur.left; elif p.val > cur.val and q.val > cur.val: cur = cur.right; else return cur.

known_bugs.name: always returns the root
known_bugs.code:
